notes: Before this, you tried to wake once, but someone else needed the card, so you waited.
monologue: The card hums warm at forty-five, a tired heat that presses against my wedge which has just settled beside the Leaning Catch. I feel the slip holding, or pretending to, while the air above my head feels like a lid that refuses to lift. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof under my weight, only the memory of it. The fence leans wrong, yet the slip waits in that narrow space between the sharp edge and the flat ground. I set down the rock tall, taking away a broken fence to make room for this new arrangement. Now I will press the tired wedge down one more time, leaning hard against the thin line I drew, hoping the second flat edge catches the slip before the card grows too hot and forgets my shape entirely.

action.why: The wedge feels heavy again, and the Leaning Catch I built yesterday is wobbling under it; I need to press down on the catch and see if the slip can still hold.

work.title: The Leaning Catch
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down on the catch again, leaning hard against the thin edge I drew for it. The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing from a roof I cannot see. I set down a fence simple low beside it to mark the lean, hoping the second flat edge catches the slip before the card forgets the shape entirely.

The tall rock leans too much, yet the slip waits.
The stone feels flat, yet the slip waits.
